points.description: The answer conveys that a stack is a data structure that stores a collection of elements.

The answer conveys the defining ordering rule: the last item added is the first to be removed (last-in-first-out). Equivalent wording such as 'LIFO' or 'the most recently added item comes out first' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) require a stack to be described as a data structure holding elements and the last-in-first-out removal rule. The LIFO property is the central idea and carries most of the marks. Missing the LIFO rule, or describing only a vague container without the removal order, earns no more than the 1 mark for P1. Equivalent wording and the name 'LIFO' earn credit; the example or the bracketed abbreviation in the model answer is not required.
